To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the visual system has to be invariant with respect to translation and scale changes and has to use a multiresolution representation.

(1) the optimal coding of visual scenes is achieved by a multiscaling code; (2) the multiscaling code is the only code that is both statistically optimal and scale invariant; and (3) the multiscalling code possesses properties that are shared by real visual systems, namely the presence of a logarithmic scale in the receptive fields of the neurons, a scale invariance in the receptive fields and a multiscaling in the receptive fields.

(i) the optimal code for vision is scale invariant and multiscaling; (ii) the scale invariance is achieved through an octave bandpass filtering; and (iii) the multiscaling is achieved through a multiresolution decomposition.
